theme: At a Traditional Thai Massage Shop

example.thai: เมื่อยคอกับไหล่มากครับ
example.phonetic: mûay kho̜o gàp lài mâak khráp
example.english: My neck and shoulders are very stiff and sore.

words.note: Use 'mûay' for muscular aches or stiffness from sitting or exercise, distinct from sharp pain ('jèp') or general illness.

example.thai: ขอนวดไทยสองชั่วโมงครับ
example.phonetic: khǒ̜o nûat thai sǒ̜ong chûa-moong khráp
example.english: I would like a two-hour Thai massage, please.

words.note: Combine with service types to specify what you want, e.g., 'nûat thai' (Thai massage) or 'nûat tháo' (foot massage).

example.thai: ช่วยนวดหนักอีกนิดได้ไหมครับ
example.phonetic: chûay nûat nàk èek nít dâai mǎi khráp
example.english: Could you please massage a bit firmer?

words.note: While 'nàk' literally means heavy, in a massage context it asks for deeper, stronger pressure.

example.thai: ขอเบามือหน่อยครับ
example.english: Please go a bit gentler with your hands.

words.note: Saying 'bao bao' or 'bao meu' immediately lets the masseuse know the current pressure is too intense.

example.thai: เจ็บเกินไปครับ

words.note: Don't suffer in silence—saying 'jèp' firmly alerts the therapist to ease off a sensitive tendon or bone.
